ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark-free quality rater from LLM-written scores on web documents in 12 languages
PROPOSAL: Sample 20000 Common Crawl documents per language for 12 languages and have an open instruction-tuned model, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, score each on educational value from 0 to 5 with one fixed rubric. Train a lightweight head on frozen multilingual E5 embeddings to regress these scores, with a held-out split of 10 percent per language. Report Spearman correlation with the teacher on the held-out split, per language, plus inference throughput in documents per second on one accelerator.
CONTROLS: Compare against a FastText classifier trained with the same teacher labels, against a perplexity filter from a small multilingual model, and against a random score. Check no benchmark text enters the training data by 13-gram overlap.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: The head should reach correlation of about 0.8 with the teacher in high-resource languages and fall for low-resource ones; the head could inherit the teacher's preference for formal registers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-student rating of multilingual web text with a long list of languages and teacher prompts
PROPOSAL: Sample 100000 Common Crawl documents for each of 30 languages and score each with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a set of rubric wordings on a 0 to 5 scale. Train heads of 3 depths on frozen multilingual E5 embeddings to regress each teacher-rubric score, with a held-out split per language. Report Spearman correlation with the teacher per language, and measure inference throughput per head on one accelerator, plus agreement between the rubric wordings.
CONTROLS: Compare against FastText classifiers trained on the same labels and against a perplexity filter. Check for benchmark overlap by 13-gram matching on the evaluation suites.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: Correlation should be high in the largest languages and drop in the lowest-resource ones; the rubric wordings could yield correlated but not identical rankings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Language-invariance of a quality rater measured on parallel documents
PROPOSAL: Build a parallel evaluation set of 5000 English documents and their machine translations into 9 languages with NLLB-200, then run a multilingual quality rater on every version. Measure, for each document, the standard deviation of the rating across language versions, and report the mean over documents together with the rank correlation between English and each translation. Train two raters, one on the original English labels alone and one on pooled labels from 9 languages, and compare invariance.
CONTROLS: Compare with a rater applied to translations back into English as a control for translation noise, and with a language-identity probe on rater embeddings to quantify how much language information remains.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The pooled rater should show lower variation across versions than the English-only one; translation noise could keep rank correlations around 0.85 in both.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-language consistency of rater scores on a translated corpus with a long series of trained raters
PROPOSAL: Build a parallel evaluation set of 20000 English documents with translations into 9 languages by NLLB-200, and apply multilingual quality raters to each version. Train 12 raters differing in label source, encoder checkpoint and pooling choice, each on English labels alone or on pooled labels from 9 languages. Measure the standard deviation of the rating over language versions per document and the rank correlation between English and each translation, per rater, then tabulate every pair of raters and the spread of ratings per language pair.
CONTROLS: Compare with a rater applied to back-translations into English, and with language-identity probes on the embeddings of all raters, then rank the raters by consistency.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Pooled-label raters should be more consistent than English-only ones; the raters could differ more by encoder than by label source.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Downstream effect of quality-based selection on a 1.2 billion parameter model in English and eight other languages
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 1.2 billion parameter decoder models on 60 billion tokens each from three mixtures of the same 9-language web pool: random selection, the top 20 percent by a multilingual quality rater, and a heuristic filter with deduplication. Evaluate with 0-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, ARC, MMLU and their translations (XCOPA, Global-MMLU), average per language group, and report differences with bootstrap intervals over tasks. One run per mixture with one seed.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on FineWeb-Edu-style English-only selection, and check selected data does not overlap evaluation sets by 13-gram matching. Keep the token count at 60 billion and the peak learning rate fixed for each mixture.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The rater mixture should lift average accuracy by one to two points over random in English and in non-English groups; the gain could shrink for the lowest-resource languages where selection removes most data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining study of quality-selected multilingual web data with a ladder of model scales and selection thresholds
PROPOSAL: Pretrain decoder models at four scales from 0.4 to 2.4 billion parameters on 60 billion tokens from six mixtures of one 9-language web pool: random selection, a heuristic filter with deduplication, and four fractions of the pool chosen by a multilingual quality rater. Evaluate 0-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, ARC, MMLU, XCOPA and Global-MMLU, averaged per language group, and report differences with bootstrap intervals over tasks, with 2 seeds for small models.
CONTROLS: Compare against English-only selection in the style of FineWeb-Edu, and check overlap with evaluation sets by 13-gram matching. Keep schedules identical in the runs.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Gains should grow with selection strength up to the top 20 percent; the bigger models could show narrower differences because they absorb noise better.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensembling judges from different LLM families to reduce model-specific bias in quality labels
PROPOSAL: Score 10000 English and 10000 multilingual documents with three judges from different families (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-it) using one rubric on a 0 to 5 scale. Measure pairwise Spearman agreement among judges and fit a mean-of-ranks ensemble label. Train one head on the ensemble labels and one head per judge on frozen embeddings, and compare how much each head's top-20-percent selection overlaps with the others.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity filter and with a random score as overlap references, and verify on 300 documents with human review that ensemble labels are not worse than single-judge labels.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Pairwise agreement should sit around 0.6, with the ensemble selecting a core shared by all judges; overlap could remain low in languages where one judge is clearly weaker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Agreement structure among six LLM judges used as quality raters on a mixed-language document set
PROPOSAL: Score 40000 English and 40000 multilingual documents with six judges (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and instruction-tuned models from the Gemma, Mistral, Phi and Aya families) using 4 rubric wordings on a 0 to 5 scale. Measure pairwise Spearman agreement and fit a mean-of-ranks ensemble label per wording. Train a head on each ensemble and one per judge on frozen embeddings, then compare the overlap of top-20-percent selections for all pairs.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity filter and with a random score as overlap references, and verify on 600 documents by human review that ensemble labels are not worse than single-judge labels.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Agreement should sit near 0.6 and overlaps should be moderate; the six judges could split into families whose members agree more among themselves.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decontamination audit of a rater trained without benchmark-derived supervision
PROPOSAL: Select the top 10 percent of a 9-language web pool with a rater trained on teacher scores, and with a rater trained like FineWeb2-HQ on benchmark positives, using 2 evaluation languages first. Count, for each language, the fraction of test items from XNLI, XCOPA, Global-MMLU and MLQA whose 13-grams appear in the selected text, against the unselected pool. Train two 0.5 billion parameter models on each selection for 20 billion tokens and compare the accuracy gap between seen and unseen test items.
CONTROLS: Compare with random selection as the base overlap rate, and shuffle the benchmark positives to confirm overlap comes from the supervision itself.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The benchmark-supervised selection should show higher overlap and an accuracy edge on seen items; the teacher-based selection could still show some overlap through shared web sources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contamination check of two selection methods at four thresholds and with six evaluation suites
PROPOSAL: Select four fractions of a 9-language web pool, from 5 up to 40 percent, with a teacher-score rater and with a rater trained like FineWeb2-HQ on benchmark positives. Count, per language, the fraction of test items from XNLI, XCOPA, Global-MMLU, MLQA, PAWS-X and MGSM whose 13-grams appear in the selected text. Train 0.5 billion parameter models on each selection for 20 billion tokens and compare accuracy between seen and unseen test items. Report each count with its bootstrap interval.
CONTROLS: Compare with random selection as the base overlap rate, and shuffle benchmark positives. Rerun the overlap count with 8-gram and 20-gram matching.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Benchmark-supervised selection should show higher overlap at all thresholds; strict matching lengths could change the absolute rates but not the ordering.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Topic coverage of quality-filtered multilingual pretraining data and its link to downstream accuracy
PROPOSAL: Cluster 5 million documents per language for 9 languages into 500 topics using multilingual embeddings, then compare topic entropy of three selections of the top 20 percent: random, by a multilingual rater, and by perplexity under a small language model. Train 1 billion parameter models on 40 billion tokens from each selection and report accuracy on 8 downstream tasks per language group, relating accuracy to topic entropy.
CONTROLS: Compare against a rater with a topic-balanced resampling step, to test whether coverage rather than quality explains the gains, and against deduplicated random selection.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: Perplexity selection should lose topic entropy and score lowest; balanced resampling could close part of the gap between the rater and random selection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Selection fraction and diversity in multilingual pretraining data: topic coverage with quality filtering
PROPOSAL: Group web documents in 9 languages by embedding similarity into topic clusters at 3 granularities and measure how each of 5 selections spreads over them: random, a multilingual rater, perplexity, a DCLM-style classifier and a rater with balanced resampling. Pretrain 1 billion parameter models on 40 billion tokens from each selection with 3 seeds, score 8 downstream tasks per language group, and report the correlation between coverage entropy and accuracy per granularity.
CONTROLS: Compare against deduplicated random selection, and report entropy with bootstrap intervals over documents. Rank the 5 selections by each statistic and plot entropy against accuracy per selection.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: Perplexity selection should lose the most coverage; entropy at the finest granularity could be noisy for languages with few documents.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling an LLM quality judge into a small multilingual scorer fast enough for a web-scale crawl
PROPOSAL: Distil Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct scores on 2 million documents in 15 languages into a 100 million parameter multilingual encoder (mMiniLM), trained to regress the 0 to 5 score for 3 epochs. Report Spearman correlation on a held-out set of 50000 documents per language group, and throughput in documents per second on one accelerator against the teacher. Estimate the time to score 1 trillion tokens at the measured throughput.
CONTROLS: Compare with a 10 million parameter FastText student and with a frozen-embedding linear head, both trained on the same teacher scores, and with a student trained on the English portion only.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The student should keep a correlation around 0.85 at several hundred times the throughput; the student could degrade on scripts that are rare in the pretraining of the encoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Student scorers of four encoder widths distilled from LLM judgments on a corpus of 30 languages
PROPOSAL: Distil Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct scores on 8 million documents in 30 languages into encoders of four widths from 20 to 600 million parameters (mMiniLM, XLM-R), each trained to regress the 0 to 5 score. Report Spearman correlation on a held-out set of 100000 documents per language group, and throughput in documents per second on one accelerator against the teacher. Estimate the time to score 1 trillion tokens per size.
CONTROLS: Compare with FastText students and with a frozen-embedding linear head on the same teacher scores, and with students trained on the English portion only.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Correlation should rise slowly with size beyond 100 million parameters; the largest students could cost more per document than their gain justifies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of a quality rater to languages unseen in its training set
PROPOSAL: Train a multilingual quality rater on teacher scores for 10 languages, then apply it without change to 10 further languages from other families, covering 5 scripts: Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari and Han. Measure Spearman correlation with fresh teacher scores on 2000 documents per unseen language and compare it to a rater trained on those languages directly. Report the correlation drop against typological distance from the nearest training language.
CONTROLS: Compare with a rater trained on English only and with a script-level heuristic filter. Add a rater whose training set includes 2 languages from each unseen family.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The drop should grow with typological distance; the drop could be small for languages that share a script with training languages, so script and family are hard to separate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Out-of-distribution behaviour of language-agnostic scorers on an extended list of low-resource languages
PROPOSAL: Fit a multilingual quality scorer on teacher labels from 10 languages, then leave it frozen and run it on 25 further languages drawn from other families, spanning Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, Ethiopic and Han scripts. Score 8000 documents per unseen language, correlate with fresh teacher labels, and set the result beside scorers trained on each of those languages directly with 4 encoder checkpoints. Plot the drop against typological distance from the closest training language.
CONTROLS: Add comparisons with scorers trained on English alone and with a script filter. Fit scorers whose training sets contain 1, 2 and 4 languages from each unseen family.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The drop should grow with typological distance; script and family may be hard to separate among the 100 trained scorer-language combinations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does a multilingual quality rater cost English accuracy compared with English-only selection
PROPOSAL: Select the top 25 percent of an English web pool with three raters: the FineWeb-Edu classifier, a DCLM-style FastText classifier, and a multilingual rater trained on teacher scores in 12 languages. Pretrain 1.2 billion parameter models on 30 billion English tokens from each selection and from random selection, and evaluate on MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag and 5 other English tasks with 0-shot accuracy. Report accuracy differences against random selection with bootstrap intervals over tasks, using one seed.
CONTROLS: Compare with a heuristic-filtered and deduplicated baseline, and check overlap with evaluation sets by 13-gram matching. Hold token count at 30 billion and the peak learning rate at 3e-4.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The multilingual rater should land within half a point of the English classifiers; the multilingual rater could trail on knowledge-heavy tasks where English-specific rubrics help.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: English-only evaluation of rater selections with a ladder of model sizes and token counts
PROPOSAL: Select the top 25 percent of an English web pool with three raters: the FineWeb-Edu classifier, a DCLM-style FastText classifier and a multilingual rater trained on teacher scores in 12 languages. Pretrain decoder models at four scales up to 2.4 billion parameters on token counts up to 60 billion English tokens, from each selection and from random selection, with 2 seeds, and score 0-shot accuracy on MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag and other tasks. Report accuracy against random selection with bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Compare with a heuristic-filtered, deduplicated baseline and check overlap by 13-gram matching. Hold the peak learning rate at 3e-4 in each run.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Differences should be small and stable across sizes; the 15 billion token count could be too short to separate the raters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native-speaker validation of rater scores in six languages
PROPOSAL: Sample 100 documents per language from 6 languages (Hindi, Swahili, Arabic, Vietnamese, Polish and Indonesian), with scores spread over the whole 0 to 5 range of a multilingual rater. Two native speakers per language rate the educational value of each document on the same 0 to 5 rubric, and report their agreement by Cohen's kappa and the Spearman correlation between their mean and the rater score. Compute both for the LLM teacher and for the distilled rater.
CONTROLS: Compare against a perplexity score and a random score as reference correlations, and verify annotators on 20 shared documents to confirm the rubric is read the same way in all languages.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Correlation with annotators should be about 0.6 for the rater and lower for perplexity; agreement among annotators could limit the ceiling in languages with fewer documents of high quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Annotator study of rater scores in twelve languages with a broad sampling design and four rater variants
PROPOSAL: Sample 400 documents per language from 12 languages with scores spread over the whole 0 to 5 range of a multilingual rater, then ask 3 native speakers per language to rate the educational value of each document on a 0 to 5 rubric. Report agreement by Cohen's kappa and the Spearman correlation between the annotator mean and the scores of the LLM teacher, the distilled rater, a FastText rater and a perplexity score, with confidence intervals by bootstrap over documents, plus weighted kappa on ordinal ratings.
CONTROLS: Compare against a random score as a reference, and verify annotators on 60 shared documents to confirm the rubric is read alike in the languages.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Correlation with annotators should be about 0.6 with this rater; kappa among 3 annotators could vary with language and with document length.
